definitions.explanation: A general term for green leafy vegetables used in cooking, such as spinach, komatsuna, bok choy, and similar greens.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}に{青菜|あおな}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I added leafy greens to the miso soup.

examples.japanese: {青菜|あおな}は{栄養|えいよう}が{豊富|ほうふ}なので、{毎日|まいにち}の{食事|しょくじ}に{取|と}り{入|い}れたい。
examples.english: Leafy greens are nutritious, so I want to include them in my daily meals.

notes:
A collective term for green leafy vegetables, combining {青|あお} (green/blue) and {菜|な} (vegetable). In Japanese cooking, {青菜|あおな} encompasses vegetables like {小松菜|こまつな}, ほうれん{草|そう}, {青梗菜|ちんげんさい}, and similar greens.

USAGE:
Commonly used in recipes and cooking contexts. When a recipe calls for {青菜|あおな}, the cook can choose whichever leafy green is available. The word also appears in the proverb {青菜|あおな}に{塩|しお} (lit. 'salt on greens'), meaning to look wilted or dejected.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {青菜|あおな}の{炒|いた}め{物|もの} — stir-fried greens
- {青菜|あおな}のおひたし — blanched greens in broth
- {青菜|あおな}に{塩|しお} — looking dejected (idiom)

RELATED WORDS:
- {小松菜|こまつな} — komatsuna; a specific type of Japanese mustard green
- {葉物|はもの}{野菜|やさい} — leafy vegetables; a more precise synonym
- {野菜|やさい} — vegetables; the general category
